reasons: The cited clause is correctly classified as sitting at the playbook fallback rather than as a deviation: the committed lock-in is a single 12-month Initial Term (not 'longer than 12 months'), and thereafter Customer may terminate for any reason on 90 days' notice — the outer edge of the 60–90 day fallback window.

Vendor's convenience right is symmetrical, unavailable during the Initial Term, and requires 90 days' notice, so it does not hit the walk-away test (Vendor exit on fewer than 90 days). Kubient's entitlement to fees generated during the 90-day notice period is consideration for services in that window and does not exceed the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling.

No redline or comment was proposed, which is the correct treatment for a compliant/at-fallback clause; the missing pro-rata refund and inability to terminate individual Exhibits are properly noted in the rationale rather than flagged.

The failed deterministic check ('Customer convenience termination present') is a phrasing artifact — the right is expressed as 'Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice' — so it does not undercut the classification.

Minor imprecision worth noting (not disqualifying): the rationale characterizes Vendor's right as 'end-of-term only', whereas 'following the Initial Term' would also permit exit mid-renewal-term on 90 days' notice; this remains within fallback tolerance and is offset by the symmetrical benefit to Customer.
